paper_metadata.title: Effect of continuous gradient Al on high-temperature oxidation of Ni-Cr-Co based superalloys via a high-throughput method

evidence.quote: Ni-Cr-Co based superalloys

samples.canonical_name: Ni-Cr-Co based superalloy with Al gradient

evidence.quote: a Ni-Cr-Co based superalloy sample with 0 % Al at the lower layers and 2.5 % Al at the upper layers
An Al element single-gradient sample was printed using a four-channel coaxial powder feeding laser cladding system
the as-printed sample was sealed in a vacuum tube and then treated at 1150 ◦C for 24 h in a GSL-1400 × tubular furnace
the as-printed sample was sealed in a vacuum tube and then treated at 1150 ◦C for 24 h in a GSL-1400 × tubular furnace
the sample was sealed in a vacuum tube, then treated at 750 ◦C for 24 h in a tubular furnace, and finally air cooled to room temperature
the sample was placed in a crucible and subjected to air at 870 ◦C for100 h in a GSL-1400 × tubular furnace, and finally air cooled to room temperature

With 3D printing process and the same processing parameters as the high-throughput sample (with laser power 450 W), five discrete samples with different Al contents and with the size around 20*20*8 mm were prepared
the discrete samples also underwent a 1150 ◦C/24 h diffusion treatment and a 750 ◦C/24 h heat treatment
the discrete samples also underwent a 1150 ◦C/24 h diffusion treatment and a 750 ◦C/24 h heat treatment
the samples were placed in a crucible which has been dried to constant weight at high temperature and subjected to 870 ◦C/100 h oxidation in air in a box furnace
